cohort: Women undergoing primary cesarean section without medical complications or pre-existing UTIs
finding: Women who did not receive routine indwelling catheterization had earlier ambulation, shorter hospital stays, less voiding discomfort, lower UTI incidence, and less need for postoperative antibiotics.
mod_finding: Women who did not receive routine indwelling catheters during Cesarean sections had earlier ambulation, shorter hospital stays, took less time for their first void, experienced less voiding discomfort, and had a lower incidence of UTIs compared to those who did receive catheters.
